title: The Burnt Cover Revisited
premise: Freya Voss, a freelance interpreter who cleans up the linguistic wreckage of doomed peace talks, receives a call on a burner phone he buried years ago—the voice belongs to Ilse Brandt, the defector he once loved and believed dead. She is alive, held in Vienna, and offering to expose a market-manipulation scheme timed to Frankfurt's opening bell, but her handlers intend her as bait to flush out everyone who ever knew her. Freya must assemble the ragtag team of exiles and fixers who became his found family, extract Ilse before dawn, and choose between burning his own cover forever or letting her die for the greater calm. In the end, he trades his invisibility for her freedom, exposing the operation at the cost of the life he built—and gaining, for the first time, one worth keeping.
about_author: Jude Sandoval is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where treaties went to die. They write thrillers about the people paid to be forgotten.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Wrapping a failed Geneva delegation, Freya buries another identity when a number he destroyed six years ago lights up his burner. The voice is Ilse's—dead Ilse. Emotional beat: dread cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Rule
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He traces the call to a Vienna relay and breaks his first rule: he answers a second time. Ilse gives him ninety seconds of coded instructions before the line dies. Emotional beat: hope arriving like an infection.

chapters.title: People Who Owe Me
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He canvasses his found family: Tomas the forger in Marseille, Ruth the retired analyst, Denny the driver who asks no questions. Each refuses, then relents. Emotional beat: reluctant loyalty rekindled.

chapters.title: What Frankfurt Opens
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth decodes Ilse's cipher: a coordinated short position rigged to detonate when markets open Friday, masked inside a legitimate peace-delegation portfolio. Emotional beat: intellectual terror—the scale of it.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. If Ilse is real, she may be chummed water; her handlers want every ghost from her past to surface. Freya weighs love against tradecraft and chooses to go anyway. Emotional beat: guilty resolve.

chapters.title: Vienna, Off Season
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Arriving under a new passport, Freya works a delegation reception to map the security detail around Ilse's safehouse. He spots a face from his buried past watching him. Emotional beat: hunted stillness.

chapters.title: Old Names, New Guns
chapters.summary: Watcher's POV (Kessler). Introduce Kessler, the counterintelligence officer who once trained Freya, now running the trap. He lets Freya see him deliberately. Emotional beat: patient menace.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds Again
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Inside the safehouse, Ilse plays her own long game, feeding her captors just enough truth. A second burner call: she tells Freya the extraction window and admits she used him six years ago. Emotional beat: love braided with betrayal.

chapters.title: Tomas Makes Three
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas arrives with papers that make Freya a delegation security consultant—access bought with a favor Tomas will never name. Emotional beat: friendship priced honestly.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The team walks the extraction: service tunnel, shift change, a decoy convoy. Denny finds a second surveillance net nobody budgeted for. Emotional beat: confidence curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: Kessler's Offer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Kessler corners Freya over coffee: walk away, keep your covers, and Ilse lives—as leverage. Freya realizes Kessler needs the scheme to succeed too. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Half Truths at Midnight
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya confesses to the team that Ilse burned him before; Ruth calls out that he's protecting himself, not them. The family fractures. Emotional beat: honesty as a wound.

chapters.title: The Tunnel
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Extraction night begins. The tunnel route is clean until a motion sensor trips early—someone moved the timeline. Emotional beat: adrenaline and suspicion in equal measure.

chapters.title: Ilse, Unscripted
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Freed but wary, Ilse reveals the deeper layer: she came back deliberately, carrying proof that names Kessler's paymasters. She never intended to be rescued quietly. Emotional beat: fury and admiration colliding.

chapters.title: Convoy of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. The decoy run goes wrong; Denny takes the pursuit so the others can slip east, buying time with a wrecked car and a broken arm. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Holed up near Bratislava, they count hours to Frankfurt's opening bell and realize the scheme doesn't need Ilse silenced—it needs her discredited. Emotional beat: the trap reshaping itself around them.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth discovers how Kessler tracked them: a beacon inside Tomas's forged documents, planted under duress—his unnamed favor called in. Emotional beat: betrayal that hurts because it was coerced.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya offers Kessler a trade: the proof, public, in exchange for Ilse's clean exit—but Kessler counters with Freya's own buried file. Emotional beat: two men negotiating with each other's souls.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs intercut. As Frankfurt opens, Ilse broadcasts the evidence through a delegation feed while markets lurch; Kessler's handlers cut him loose mid-call. Emotional beat: chaos as liberation.

chapters.title: The Price Tag
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The scheme collapses, but Freya's covers burn one by one—passports voided, aliases flagged. He becomes officially nobody, hunted by paperwork instead of guns. Emotional beat: grief for a self he never liked anyway.

chapters.title: Nobody's Home
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse, granted quiet asylum through testimony, waits at a border crossing not sure he'll come. Freya arrives with nothing but a duffel bag and a real name spoken aloud for the first time in years. Emotional beat: vulnerability as arrival.

chapters.title: The Unburnt Page
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. Months later, the scattered family regathers in a coastal town—Denny driving, Tomas forging wedding invitations, Ruth fact-checking the menu. Freya keeps one burner phone, switched off, in a drawer. Emotional beat: peace chosen, not inherited.
